Nonribosomal Peptides, Key Biocontrol Components for Pseudomonas fluorescens In5, Isolated from a Greenlandic Suppressive Soil

>

Potatoes are cultivated in southwest Greenland without the use of pesticides and with limited crop rotation. Despite the fact that plant-pathogenic fungi are present, no severe-disease outbreaks have yet been observed.

For me, this is one of the most interesting topics in soil microbiology. First off, there's more and more newly discovered territories of cultured soil, where certain pathogens never threaten the crop, even though they are present. Hence the term suppressive soil. In most parts of Greenland they don't even need to use pesticides to grow potatoes apparently, that's amazing! But as they dug deeper, they eventually found a biocontrol agent (be it bacteria or fungi) that was responsible for the inhibition. Majority of research in this field is focused on finding and harnessing this microorganisms in suppressive soils in hopes to find alternatives to current chemical pesticide overload.

The second best thing is the mechanism these agents use. In most cases the bioactive compound is a nonribosomal peptide, a protein synthesized by way of NRPS enzyme and not traditional ribosomes/mRNA, which leads to identification of novel and in some cases very potent substances, which also show great prospect in the development of new antibiotics.
